clue.text: Young people's noise putting strain on father?

blocks.note: pop is an informal word for a dad
a strain is a passage of melody

explanation.surface: A teenager's racket wears down a weary dad's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain on father' reads as stress for Dad, but it is a tune placed after the word for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Chart songs aimed at teenagers are what an older generation dismissively calls youngsters' noise.

clue.text: Stare down from striking clock

blocks.note: workers on strike are out
a clock face, or slang for a face itself

explanation.surface: A chiming clock's sound makes you look away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking clock' suggests chimes; striking is industrial action, and clock is slang for a face as well as having one.
explanation.definitionFit: To outface someone is to defeat them by confronting them boldly, looking them down until they yield.

clue.text: Old weapon found in church in spa

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: Matlock is a Derbyshire spa town
CH is the standard short form of church

explanation.surface: An antique gun is discovered inside a church at a resort town.
explanation.walkthrough: Matlock Bath is a spa resort in the English county of Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchlock is an early musket fired by lowering a slow-burning cord onto the powder pan.

clue.text: Field the ball

blocks.note: first meaning: an area of activity or expertise
second meaning: a perfectly round solid object

explanation.surface: A cricket captain's instruction to stop a hit shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' reads as the verb to stop a ball in cricket; it is the noun for a domain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a domain of interest or influence and a round globe-shaped body.

clue.text: Source of programmes not obtainable by the wireless

definitions.text: Source of programmes not obtainable by the wireless

blocks.clueFragment: Source of programmes not obtainable by the wireless
blocks.note: surface reading: shows you cannot pick up on a radio set
setter's reading: a service that needs a wire, delivered by underground line rather than broadcast

explanation.surface: A complaint that some broadcasts can't be received on the old radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Wireless is the old British word for a radio; the joke is that this service arrives through a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: This service delivers channels to subscribers through buried lines instead of over the airwaves.

clue.text: Drunk and revolting notable

blocks.note: high means intoxicated
people in revolt are said to be up in arms, or simply up

explanation.surface: A dignitary is caught tipsy and behaving disgracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' suggests disgusting, but here it means rising in rebellion, as in 'the people are up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-up is an informal noun for a person of senior rank or importance, a notable figure.

clue.text: Fair and square, initially, in accommodation

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word before it is used
in means the preceding pieces sit inside the following word

blocks.note: a home is somewhere to live
taken as written
the opening letter of square

explanation.surface: Lodgings described as fair and square, honest dealing over a rental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair and square' looks like one phrase, but fair is the definition and 'and' is used literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means good-looking or attractive, which is what handsome means.

clue.text: The bed of the sea

blocks.note: surface reading: the ocean floor
setter's reading: the hanging sleeping place a sailor uses aboard ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed of the sea' is a set phrase for the seabed; read literally it is where seamen sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors traditionally slept in slung canvas cots strung between beams below deck.

clue.text: American investigator's more radical style

blocks.note: pink means mildly left-wing, so more radical is pinker
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A US private eye with an extreme, left-leaning way of working.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton, from French, is an old word for fashionable style. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Pinkerton founded the US detective agency, and its operatives were called Pinkertons.

clue.text: Painful side-effect that's produced by needle

blocks.note: first meaning: a sharp cramp in your side when running
second meaning: a loop of thread made in sewing

explanation.surface: A medical warning that an injection may leave an unpleasant after-effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side-effect' sounds medical, but it is literally an effect felt in the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sudden ache under the ribs during exercise and a single loop of sewing thread.

clue.text: Tribesman's predicament in African country

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside that word's letters

blocks.note: Benin is a West African state
a jam is a tight spot

explanation.surface: A tribal man finds himself in trouble somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, so a member of it is a Benjamin, or Benjamite. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Benjamin is both Jacob's youngest son and the Israelite tribe descended from him, so a tribesman fits.

clue.text: Veteran in Copenhagen, say

blocks.note: first meaning: an old campaigner who has seen many battles
second meaning: Copenhagen was the Duke of Wellington's charger at Waterloo

explanation.surface: An old soldier living in the Danish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Copenhagen looks like the city, but it is the famous horse Wellington rode at Waterloo; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An old warhorse is a seasoned veteran of many fights, and a cavalry mount ridden into battle is literally one.

clue.text: Dancer getting male so excited

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A performer whose dancing gets a man very worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Salome danced for Herod and asked for John the Baptist's head as her reward, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome is the Biblical figure famed for her dance of the seven veils before King Herod.

clue.text: Loads put on male slave

indicators.note: one word put on another is placed after it in the line

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
a lot means loads, a great deal

explanation.surface: Heavy burdens are piled on a man in servitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta, so the word means a bondsman or serf.

clue.text: Book made from stiff paper

blocks.note: hard means rigid, stiff
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A volume manufactured from rigid card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff paper' reads as card, but paper is a newspaper, and here the setter's own.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is a novel by Charles Dickens set in an industrial northern town.

clue.text: Different, and fair game

blocks.note: new means not the same as before
a fair is a market or trade gathering

explanation.surface: Something unusual, and a sporting chance to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' looks like a phrase meaning a legitimate target, but fair is a market and game is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a card game in which players lay cards in sequence on stake cards, as well as a racing town.

clue.text: Preliminary version using coarse actors

blocks.note: rough means coarse
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A first draft of a play staged with crude, unpolished performers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a roughcast is a first outline or draft of a plan or story, not yet refined.

clue.text: Resign when county supports measure

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: a step is a measure taken, a course of action
County Down is in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An official quits once the local council backs a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is the common idiom for leaving a post voluntarily, which is to resign.

clue.text: Criminal always follows what's handled in court

indicators.note: the word that follows comes after the other one

blocks.note: a tennis racket is gripped on the court
e'er is the poetic short form of ever

explanation.surface: A crook is forever trailing the evidence presented at his trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law, but it is the tennis court where the racket is held.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest or illegal business such as extortion, so he is a criminal.

clue.text: Section of church a lot left

blocks.note: a lot is a chance, as in casting lots
L is the short form of left

explanation.surface: A large part of the church has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot left' reads as plenty remaining; lot is a draw of fortune and left is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area round the altar at the east end of a church, kept for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Plant's on the way, roughly speaking

blocks.note: something on the way is coming

explanation.surface: A gardener announcing that a seedling is about to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Dropping the final g of coming, as in casual speech, gives the spice's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is an umbellifer grown for its aromatic seeds, used as a spice in curries.

clue.text: Man, for example, is so narrow minded

blocks.note: first meaning: the Isle of Man is an island, so it is of that nature
second meaning: inward-looking and parochial

explanation.surface: A complaint that men in general are blinkered.
explanation.walkthrough: Man here is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, not mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to an island, and figuratively cut off from outside ideas, hence parochial.

clue.text: Liberal opponent of Tory said to be an important person

blocks.note: liberal means generous, as in a big helping
the Whigs were the historic rivals of the Tories

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician, rival of the Conservatives, is reckoned a heavyweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' and 'Tory' suggest politics throughout, but Liberal is just generous; only the Whig is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is informal for a person of high rank or influence, from the large wigs once worn by dignitaries.

clue.text: Possible location of storm in China?
